subject: Follow-up: token economics, procurement constraints & pilot framing — Wireframe Labs discovery
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Wong <emily.wong@wireframe.com>, Mark Lim <mark.lim@wireframe.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 May 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: token economics, procurement constraints & pilot framing — Wireframe Labs discovery

Hi Emily / Mark — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Key pain / goals you shared:
- Token spend sensitivity: core NLU calls spike ~3x during peak hours and procurement has a hard cap of ~$75k / month for model consumption.
- Latency requirement for triage path: p95 < 250ms for short prompts (under 256 tokens). Some lower-priority pathways can accept higher latency.
- Compliance / procurement asks: SOC 2 evidence, data residency note (US-only), and a standard SLA for pilot (uptime + incident response).

Redwood levers we covered that impact TCO:
- Batching + request shaping: continuous batching for long-running flows; expect ~20–40% token cost reduction on inference tokens for batched user journeys.
- Prefix/KV caching for repeat queries (search/FAQ paths) to reduce model calls ~30–60% depending on hit rate.
- Quantized model variants: 8-bit or 4-bit weights for lower-cost inference on some routes; slight accuracy trade-offs (we’ll benchmark on your prompts).
- Smart routing: route non-critical traffic to lower-cost variants, keep critical pathways on low-latency variants.

Proposed pilot scope (6 weeks):
1) Kickoff + SOW: baseline metrics collection (1 week) — share sample prompt set and usage profile.
2) Pilot run (4 weeks): deploy hybrid routing + caching; run both high-quality and low-cost variants to measure delta.
3) Readout & recommended runbook (1 week): cost model, latency/eval results, ops checklist for rollout.

Deliverables we’ll provide this week:
- Redesigned pilot MOP (attached: redwood_pilot_mop_v1.pdf)
- Initial cost model template (attached: wireframe_cost_model_v1.xlsx)
- SOC 2 artifacts pointer and procurement checklist

Asks from your side:
- Confirm budget envelope for pilot vs. production ($75k/mo noted) and procurement timeline.
- Share sample prompt traffic and representative dataset for accuracy benchmarking.
- Introduce procurement contact (procurement@wireframe.com) so we can share SOC 2 docs.

Next steps (action owners):
- Diego: update cost model with your traffic profile (I’ll take the first pass once we get sample logs).
- Hannah (SE): scope quantization/latency trade-off evals and suggested config.
- Mark / Emily: confirm procurement contact and internal approver for pilot commitment.

If that aligns, I’ll schedule a 30-minute kickoff next week (Hannah + Jordan + your technical lead).

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_pilot_mop_v1.pdf, wireframe_cost_model_v1.xlsx

From: Emily Wong <emily.wong@wireframe.com>

Cc: Mark Lim <mark.lim@wireframe.com>, procurement@wireframe.com
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: token economics, procurement constraints & pilot framing — Wireframe Labs discovery

Thanks Diego — this is super helpful and captures the call. Couple clarifications from our side: 

- Budget: procurement has approved up to $75k/month for a pilot if we can demonstrate >= 30% cost improvement on the most frequent flows (customer support triage & billing lookups).
- Timeline: procurement is on a 3-week review cycle for pilots; we’d like kickoff before May 21 to get through procurement by mid-June.
- SOC / security: procurement@wireframe.com is looped. They’ll send a standard questionnaire; can you confirm which SOC artifacts you’ll provide? (we need control plane SOC2 + any host/cloud provider attestations).
- Latency: p95 < 250ms is a hard requirement for triage. For the lower-priority batch processes we can tolerate p95 <= 1s.

We’ll also attach the procurement questionnaire in a separate email (procurement@wireframe.com). I’ve attached a short sample traffic extract to this reply for your modeling (wireframe_sample_traffic.csv).

Emily
Emily Wong
Head of Product, Wireframe Labs
Attachments: wireframe_sample_traffic.csv

From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Wireframe pilot — cost posture and ask list (private)

Hannah / Jordan — forwarding the thread and adding internal notes. High-level read:

- Opportunity: mid-market payments vertical; if pilot shows ~30% token cost reduction on customer support flows we can move to a 12-month committed Dedicated deal.
- Constraints: strict $75k/month procurement cap for initial pilot; SOC2 + US data residency.

Initial recommended approach (we’ll iterate):
1) Pilot pricing: 6-week pilot on a pre-paid consumption cap of $40k (covers baseline + expected overage headroom). If we demonstrate >=30% reduction we convert to a committed proposal. This gives them a lower upfront vote-of-confidence.
2) Tech approach: prioritize caching + routing for FAQ/lookup flows (high hit rate expected) + quantized variant A/B for triage route. Run parallel evaluation to capture accuracy/latency tradeoffs.
3) Deliverables for kickoff: one-pager MOP, cost scenarios (10/30/50% cache hit), latency table per model variant, SOC2 artifacts link.

Hannah: can you draft the latency / accuracy table and run quick bench against the sample traffic? Target: p95 < 250ms on critical route with the low-latency variant.
Jordan: please own the commercial motion with Emily/Mark and confirm internal RD with Procurement. I’ll propose the $40k pre-pay pilot and the conversion trigger.

I’ll put the kickoff invite on calendar once Emily confirms attendees.

– Diego
